rollouts.actual_final:
The judgment in *Fedsure Life Assurance v Greater Johannesburg Transitional Metropolitan Council* was handed down on **14 October 1998**.

In 1998, South Africa had **11** official languages. This number was established by the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 (Act 108 of 1996), which came into effect on 4 February 1997. The Constitution lists the following 11 official languages: Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, English, Northern Sotho, Tswana, Southern Sotho, Tsonga, Swazi, Venda, and Ndebele. (Previously, the Interim Constitution of 1993 recognized 9 official languages).

**11**
